title: Fix: prevent control plane from marking pools Ready before perf-canary completion (transactional guard)
author: Ethan Park
description:
Why: During the Dedicated provision-to-ready pilot we observed a race where a provisioning run could transition to READY before the perf-canary job finished writing its result. In practice, this happened when the validation pipeline emitted a "validation stage complete" event and the orchestrator immediately advanced the run to READY, while perf-canary was still running (or its completion callback was delayed). Once READY propagated, routing could begin advertising the pool (depending on rollout flags) even though the perf-canary gate hadn’t actually passed yet. This manifested as a short window of intermittent 5xx / degraded performance during the validation window and was confusing for operators because the UI showed READY while perf-canary logs were still active.

What changed: This PR makes the READY transition conditional on an atomic check of gate completion. Concretely: (1) Added a transactional guard when attempting VALIDATING -> READY: we now require perf_canary_status == PASS (or perf_canary_required == false for legacy runs) in the same DB transaction as the state update. (2) Centralized the transition logic into mark_ready_if_gates_passed(...) which is called from both the validation completion handler and the perf-canary completion handler. This makes event ordering irrelevant: whichever event arrives last will be able to advance the run, but only if both gates are satisfied. (3) Added SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locking on the provisioning_run row to avoid concurrent READY transitions and ensure audit timestamps are consistent. (4) Improved the operator-facing failure message when a READY transition is attempted early: we now surface "waiting_for_perf_canary" as a distinct reason with a pointer to the Dedicated provisioning runbook.

Implementation details: The previous code path updated readiness_state to READY based solely on stage == VALIDATING and validation_result == PASS. Perf-canary wrote its result to a separate table/field and emitted an event, but we didn’t join those two concerns at the time of the READY update. The new flow stores perf_canary_status on the run record (PASS/FAIL/RUNNING/UNKNOWN) and uses a single transaction to: load+lock the run row, confirm current state is VALIDATING, confirm validation_passed == true, confirm perf_canary_status == PASS (unless perf_canary_required == false), then set readiness_state = READY and ready_at = now(). If the run is already READY/FAILED/CANCELLED, the function exits idempotently.

Testing: Added unit tests for the transition function (including idempotency and early-ready attempts) and a concurrency-ish test that simulates out-of-order callbacks (perf-canary completion arriving before validation completion, and vice versa). Also manually tested in dev by delaying the perf-canary callback and confirming the run remains in VALIDATING with reason waiting_for_perf_canary until the canary posts PASS.

Rollout/ops: Safe to roll out immediately; this tightens the gating semantics to match the intended definition of READY. Added a metric counter control_plane_ready_transition_blocked_total{reason} to help us spot any unexpected blocks after deploy (cardinality-safe). This should reduce operator confusion and prevent routing from ever seeing a pool marked READY without a completed perf-canary run.

Checklist: - [x] Added unit tests - [x] Added a small amount of new metrics (low-cardinality) - [x] Verified no schema change required (uses existing run record fields introduced in the readiness work) - [x] Added runbook pointer in the blocked transition log message
commits: control-plane: add mark_ready_if_gates_passed() helper with transactional guard
control-plane: gate VALIDATING->READY on perf_canary_status==PASS (or perf_canary_required=false)
control-plane: lock provisioning_run row during transition to avoid concurrent READY writes
metrics/logging: add blocked-ready counter + operator-facing reason waiting_for_perf_canary
tests: simulate out-of-order validation/perf-canary callbacks and assert READY only after both pass
review_conversation: Rina Kobayashi: Perf-canary has a couple of failure modes where the callback never fires (e.g., job was cancelled). Will this cause runs to get stuck in VALIDATING forever? Ethan Park: Good point. This PR doesn’t change timeouts/cancellation behavior; it just prevents premature READY. In our current workflow, a cancelled/timeout canary is already treated as FAIL and we emit a failure event that moves the run to FAILED. I added an explicit mapping: if canary status is FAIL/TIMEOUT/CANCELLED we will not mark READY and the existing failure handler will transition to FAILED with a clear reason.

Rafael Mendes: Can you confirm this is truly atomic under concurrency? We’ve seen duplicate callbacks. Ethan Park: Yes. The transition function now acquires a row lock (SELECT FOR UPDATE) and checks current readiness_state + stage before writing. Duplicate callbacks become no-ops once READY is set, and the audit log entry is only written once (guarded by the same transaction). Added a test that calls the transition twice and asserts a single READY transition event.

Miles Thornton: Please avoid adding pool_id/customer_id as metric labels. Aisha and I want something to alert on without exploding cardinality. Ethan Park: Agreed. The new metric is control_plane_ready_transition_blocked_total{reason} only. Identifiers stay in structured logs with correlation_id and pool_id for debugging.

Vikram Singh: Does this affect backward compatibility with older runs that don’t set perf_canary_status? Ethan Park: Covered. If perf_canary_required == false (legacy / staged rollout), we allow READY once validation passes. If perf_canary_required == true but status is UNKNOWN, we block and log waiting_for_perf_canary. This matches intended behavior once the perf-canary integration is enabled for that run type.

Aisha Bello: Can we add a log line that clearly says READY was deferred due to canary not completed? This would help on-call. Ethan Park: Added a structured event control_plane_ready_transition_blocked with reason=waiting_for_perf_canary and a runbook slug. It fires at INFO with rate limiting so it’s visible but not noisy.
release_notes: Fixes a race where Dedicated pools could be marked READY before perf-canary completion. READY transition is now gated by an atomic/transactional check that perf-canary has passed (when required), preventing premature routing advertisement and reducing validation-window 5xx risk.
